text:
marta: quick dump from tonight's regional sweep — noticed a sustained throughput regression on H100 in eu-west during mixed prefill+decode workload
kai: rough numbers?
marta: mosaic-7b (q8x4) and tiny-13b (q4_0) runs. baseline h100 peak ~9.2k tok/s prefill+decode, then falling to ~7.6k tok/s after ~10m under steady QPS
sahil: that's ~18% drop — any nvml/power/thermal flags in perf traces?
perf-bot: nightly-bench job 3049990000 finished. summary attached: h100-eu-west: 9.2k -> 7.6k tok/s after 10m; a100-eu-west: steady ~6.4k tok/s. nvml: 2 throttle events, fan speed ramped. kernel log: attn fused -> fallback at drop point
ingrid: so H100 still higher peak but flaky under sustained decode. A100 lower peak but steadier
kai: SKU was h100-48g-p1 (shared host). noisy neighbor or host power governor could explain it. Did kernel selection flip coincide with clock downshift?
marta: yes, kernel selection shows fused-attn -> nonfused fallback exactly when clocks step down in nvml logs
devon: can we reproduce on dedicated h100? also try different power cap settings
marta: reproduced on fresh eu-west node with same sku in lab (~22C ambient). ran 15m steady-state, saw same fallback ~10m in
sahil: cost angle: at h100 peak tokens cost ~ $68 / 1M (q8x4 7b), but after drop effective $/1M rises to ~ $85 — same as a100 baseline
ingrid: that's the risk: transient throttles turn unit-cost advantage into parity. we should bake a "sustained headroom" factor into SKU fitment guidance
kai: ops idea: run a dedicated vs shared SKU comparison and capture nvml/perf + kernel-switch telemetry. if dedicated avoids fallback we keep H100 lead
marta: proposal: add a `sustained-decoding` stage to bench harness: 15m steady-state, record nvml clocks, kernel switchpoints, host-saturation signals, and ambient temp
devon: +1. Gate Dedicated sizing recs on pass/fail of that test
sahil: also run q4_0 vs q8x4 sensitivity sweep to see quantization impact on thermals and kernel choices
perf-bot: created issue ML-thermal-scan-2026 with attached traces and raw logs
kai: if fallback is common we could auto-route sustained jobs to A100 in eu-west via policy flag (latency/cost fallback)
ingrid: add a short note in docs about ambient/host risk and suggested headroom (e.g., reserve 20% throughput cushion) :memo:
marta: I'll kick off dedicated runs tomorrow and upload perf traces + a short summary here. tagging @kai @ingrid
kai: thanks — if dedicated runs show no fallback, we should add dedicated-h100 to recommended SKUs for sustained decode workloads
marta: also will try a short powercap experiment (10% down/up) to see threshold where kernel flip triggers
sahil: plan of action: 1) dedicated h100 sustained 15m 2) dedicated a100 sustained 15m 3) q4_0 vs q8x4 sensitivity 4) update cost model and docs
marta: uploading traces when ready. :thumbsup:
